title: New Figures

description.main: New Figures presents Richard Prince's appropriated and manipulated found photographs that evoke charged imagery through drawn lines, pale washes of color, and collaged shapes. Published on the occasion of Prince's 2014 exhibition at Almine Rech Gallery in Paris, the book documents the artist's continued exploration of appropriation and transformation.
description.extended: Richard Prince's New Figures series engages with found photographs that suggest erotic content, overlaying them with elegant drawn lines, pale colors, and scissor-cut collaged shapes. The work references modernist masters—recalling Picasso's fluid contours and Matisse's paper cutouts—while maintaining Prince's characteristic appropriation strategy. The photographs are transformed through Prince's interventions, creating tension between the original source material and the artist's additions. Published by Almine Rech Editions with text by Jeff Rian, this bilingual publication documents the body of work shown at the gallery's Paris location in fall 2014. The book's modest format belies the provocative nature of the imagery, continuing Prince's decades-long investigation of American visual culture, authorship, and desire.
description.artist_bio: Richard Prince (b. 1949, Panama Canal Zone) is a seminal figure in appropriation art and a key member of the Pictures Generation that emerged in the late 1970s. Working initially as a clipper at Time Inc., Prince began rephotographing advertisements, creating his iconic Cowboys series (1980–1992) from Marlboro ads and later his Nurse Paintings (2003) from pulp novel covers. His practice has fundamentally challenged concepts of authorship, ownership, and originality in contemporary art. Prince is represented by Gagosian, Barbara Gladstone, and Almine Rech galleries. His work is held in major collections including the Museum of Modern Art, New York; Metropolitan Museum of Art; Whitney Museum of American Art; Tate, London; and Victoria and Albert Museum. He has been the subject of major retrospectives at the Whitney Museum (1992), Guggenheim Museum (2007), and Serpentine Gallery (2008).
description.exhibition_context: New Figures was exhibited at Almine Rech Gallery in Paris from October 20 to December 20, 2014. The Paris gallery, known for its program of established and emerging contemporary artists, provided an intimate setting for Prince's provocative explorations of appropriated imagery. This exhibition and publication represent Prince's ongoing engagement with found photographs and collage techniques, positioning his work within the lineage of modernist collage while maintaining his distinctly postmodern approach to image-making and authorship.
